codes.justification: The clause allocates responsibility to the Design-Builder for costs, expenses, and damages resulting from performing work known to violate laws, ordinances, rules, regulations, or codes without proper notice, establishing a clear risk allocation for non-compliance.
The clause requires the Design-Builder to correct violations of laws/codes performed knowingly, which parallels correction obligations for non-conforming work, including bearing associated costs.

The clause requires the PMT to investigate and document existing site conditions, utilities, and survey accuracy specifically to inform and support the Design Services and the Work, ensuring consistency between site conditions and design development.

This site examination occurs during the Validation Phase, prior to the Construction Phase, as part of the IPD Team's collaborative pre-construction activities feeding into the Validation Report and subsequent design/contract documents.

The clause enumerates the core duties the Design/Construction Team must perform during the Construction Phase, including performing the Work (.4), procuring subcontractors/suppliers (.2), and completing tasks needed for Ready-for-Takeover (.7), establishing broad execution obligations under the Contract Documents.
Sub-clause .1 requires the team to 'complete the remainder of the Design Services,' directly implicating coordination and consistency of design activities with the ongoing Work during construction.

The clause requires Shop Drawings to be submitted to authorities having jurisdiction for approval, which is a form of review/approval by authorized parties analogous to inspection oversight required by authorities.
The clause addresses coordination responsibilities for Shop Drawings, ensuring they meet requirements of authorities having jurisdiction as part of design documentation compatibility with the Work.

The clause comprehensively establishes and details the insurance coverages the Construction Manager must provide, maintain and pay for, including general liability, automobile, aircraft/watercraft, property, boiler and machinery, contractors' equipment, and pollution liability insurance, defining scope, insureds, and duration of coverage.

The clause allocates risk of loss or damage between the Construction Manager and Owner, including handling of insurance payments, restoration obligations, and adjustments to Contract Time, reflecting a broader risk allocation mechanism tied to insurance coverage.
The provision addresses extension of Contract Time relative to loss or damage, linking insurance-related events to schedule adjustments.

The clause governs the disposition (return or destruction) of information or documentation prepared or received before termination, addressing control over documents and implying ownership/custody rights of the preparing parties.

The clause establishes a formal mediation process, requiring parties to engage a Project Mediator under CCDC 40 rules to resolve unresolved disputes, directly matching the dispute resolution procedure definition.
The clause limits and allocates the Design-Builder's liability for claims relating to Design Services, an explicit allocation of contractual risk between the parties.
The clause ties the limitation of liability to the amount of insurance the Design-Builder is obligated to carry under GC 11.1 - INSURANCE, directly referencing insurance coverage requirements.

The clause deals explicitly with toxic or hazardous substances present at the Place of the Project and requires disposal, storage, or rendering them harmless in accordance with applicable legislation, which is an environmental obligation.
The clause allocates responsibility for pre-existing hazardous substances to the Owner, establishing an explicit risk allocation between the parties.

The clause governs the Payment Certifier's review and certification of the application for Substantial Performance, which is a payment-related certification mechanism triggering holdback release procedures under GC 5.4.
The Payment Certifier reviews the Work to verify the validity of the application for Substantial Performance, involving an inspection/verification function to confirm status of the Work.

The clause establishes the Owner's right to make changes to the Work through Change Orders or Change Directives, including additions, deletions, revisions, and adjustments to Contract Time, which is the core mechanism of the Changes in the Work code.

The clause requires the Owner to notify the Construction Manager of any material impact on the viability of the Project, which reflects managing and communicating project risk affecting the Contract's performance.
The clause governs adjustments to the Contractor's Fee resulting from changes in the Work, tying compensation changes to the change mechanism established in the Contract Documents.
The clause addresses the method of adjusting the Contractor's Fee, which is a payment-related compensation mechanism tied to changes in the Work.

This clause defines and itemizes the components of the Cost of the Work, which forms the basis for calculating and administering the Guaranteed Maximum Price or Target Cost under the cost-reimbursable structure of this Contract.

The clause establishes the categories of actual costs (labour, materials, subcontract amounts, insurance premiums, etc.) that are reimbursable to the Construction Manager, forming the substantive basis for payment applications and certification under the Contract.
The clause imposes an operational duty on the Contractor to take precautions and notify the Consultant during performance of the Work, governing how the Work is carried out when discoveries are made.
The clause grants the Consultant authority to reject work that does not conform to the Contract Documents, directly addressing identification and rejection of non-conforming work.
The clause gives the Consultant authority to require inspection or testing of work whether fabricated, installed or completed, establishing inspection rights and procedures.
The clause explicitly references non-payment of compensation for Services as a form of default, tying the termination right to failure to pay.

The clause allocates the risk of Owner non-compliance by giving the Construction Manager a contractual remedy (Notice in Writing of default) when the Owner substantially fails to meet its obligations.

This clause establishes that the Contract, once formed, constitutes a fixed baseline that can only be modified through the formal amendment mechanisms provided in the Contract Documents, reflecting the concept of a locked-in baseline subject to formal change procedures.

The clause references amendment of the Contract, which is effectuated through the Contract's change mechanisms such as Change Orders and Change Directives, tying it to the formal process for adjusting the Work and Contract Price.
The clause directly addresses whether the Owner may withhold fees due to the Construction Manager, which is a payment provision governing when fees can or cannot be withheld.

The clause relates to variance from the Construction Cost Estimate, a cost-target mechanism, and clarifies that deviation from this estimate does not trigger payment consequences, tying into the administration of the cost estimate concept.

The clause governs how completion prerequisites related to performance of the Work are handled without delaying the Ready-for-Takeover determination, establishing a requirement for how execution status is assessed under the Contract Documents.

The clause allocates the consequence of deferred prerequisites (conditions beyond the Contractor's control or by agreement) so that Ready-for-Takeover is not delayed, effectively managing risk of timing impacts arising from these deferrals.

The requirement that the Contractor stamp, date and sign Shop Drawings as evidence of review functions as a quality assurance check confirming the Contractor's verification of Product/fabrication details before submission to the Consultant.

Shop Drawings are part of the design detailing process; the Contractor's documented review ensures consistency and coordination between the Shop Drawings and the Contract Documents prior to their use in the Work.

The clause is part of Part 8 Dispute Resolution and addresses retention of rights/recourses conditioned on giving Notice in Writing under the dispute resolution provisions and following the Consultant's instructions under GC 8.1, directly relating to the dispute resolution process.
The clause allocates responsibility for loss and damage arising from termination between the parties through set off or deduction, an allocation of risk/liability tied to a defined exception process.
The clause addresses adjustment of amounts owed to a terminating party via set off or deduction, directly affecting payment entitlements.

The clause governs the mechanics of indemnification claims between parties, including notice requirements and rights of appeal, which is part of allocating and managing risk and liability under the Contract.

The clause requires the Owner to pay the Construction Manager within 28 calendar days of invoice submission for Services properly performed up to termination, addressing payment timing and certification mechanics upon termination.
The clause establishes the process for appointing a Project Mediator under the mediation and arbitration rules, forming part of the contractual dispute resolution mechanism.
The clause is part of the Stipulated Price Option appendix, tied to the exercise of the Change Order that establishes the Stipulated Price, and specifies what the price includes.

The clause assigns the Contractor responsibility for construction means, methods, techniques, and procedures, establishing a core duty governing how the Work is performed under the Contract Documents.
The clause explicitly makes the Contractor responsible for construction 'sequences' and for coordinating the various parts of the Work, directly addressing sequencing of the Work.

The clause assigns the Contractor sole responsibility for construction means, methods, techniques, sequences, and procedures, and for coordinating the various parts of the Work, establishing a core duty governing how the Work is performed and organized.
The clause explicitly references responsibility for 'sequences' of construction, addressing the order in which portions of the Work proceed.

This clause establishes a general quality standard requiring Products used in the Work to be new and of consistent quality, governing how the Work is performed in accordance with the Contract Documents.

The clause expressly addresses ownership and property rights in Specifications, Drawings, and models, stating they remain the Consultant's property except for signed Contract sets which belong to each party.

This clause is part of GC 6.6 CLAIMS FOR A CHANGE IN CONTRACT PRICE and establishes the process by which the Consultant issues findings on claims for changes in the Contract Price, which is a core mechanism of adjusting the Work/Contract Price under the change provisions.

The clause addresses the Consultant's determination that concealed conditions are not materially different and that no adjustment to the Contract Price or Contract Time is warranted, which is part of the change evaluation process under Part 6 Changes in the Work.
The clause addresses how and when payments are made to the Design-Builder in connection with insurance proceeds, tying payment mechanics to loss or damage events.
The clause expressly references property and boiler and machinery insurance policies and payments arising from covered loss or damage, directly invoking insurance coverage under GC 11.1.

The clause establishes a broader organizational condition for how the Work may be performed by allowing the Owner to have Other Contractors or its own forces perform related work in connection with the Project, which affects how the Contractor's Work is organized and executed alongside others.

The clause imposes a requirement on insurance policies, mandating that insurers be licensed in the jurisdiction of the Place of the Work, directly addressing insurance requirements under the Contract.

The clause allows either party to submit a claim for adjustment to the Contract Price when post-bid legislative or regulatory changes affect the cost of the Work, invoking the claims process under GC 6.6, which governs changes in Contract Price.

The clause requires that adjustments to Contract Price and Contract Time resulting from delays be processed through the Owner's right to make changes, Change Order, and Change Directive provisions, directly tying delay-related adjustments to the formal change mechanism.

The clause requires the Trade Contractor to correct or pay for damage resulting from corrective work performed under the warranty provisions, directly addressing consequences and responsibility for correction of defective or non-conforming Work.
The clause allocates responsibility to the Trade Contractor for damage arising from correction work, assigning risk/liability for consequential damage caused during corrective actions.

The clause ties expenditures under the contingency allowance directly to the change order and change directive mechanisms (GC 6.1, 6.2, 6.3), which govern adjustments to the Work and Contract Price through formal change procedures.

The clause explicitly directs that disputes and matters in question between the Contractor and Other Contractors be resolved under Part 8 Dispute Resolution, including deemed consent to arbitration and treatment of disputes lacking reciprocal obligations as disputes with the Owner.
The clause requires the Owner to pay the terminated party the Reimbursable Costs incurred to the date of termination, subject to set-off, directly addressing payment mechanics upon termination.
The provision allocates responsibility for loss and damage arising from the terminated party's default through a right of set-off or deduction, reflecting an allocation of contractual risk.

The clause expressly declares that fossils, artifacts, and other items of scientific or historic interest discovered at the Place of the Work are deemed the absolute property of the Owner, directly addressing ownership/title as between Owner and Contractor.
The clause establishes that the Contractor shall control, direct, and supervise the Work to ensure conformity with the Contract Documents, directly governing performance and supervision of the Work.
The clause references toxic and hazardous substances and mould, which are environmental considerations governed by specific GCs addressing environmental risks.
The clause appears under Part 6 Changes in the Work and GC 6.4 Concealed or Unknown Conditions, directing how such conditions are treated within the change provisions framework.

The clause requires the Owner and/or Trade Contractors to obtain, maintain, and pay for various specified insurance coverages (Automobile Liability, aircraft/watercraft, Contractors' Equipment, and Contractors' Pollution Liability Insurance) in accordance with CCDC 41 requirements, directly addressing insurance obligations under the Contract.

The clause requires the Consultant to issue changes required to the Contract Documents via Change Order or Change Directive when variances with applicable laws arise, directly invoking the formal change mechanisms under GC 6.1-6.3.

The clause allocates responsibility, relieving the Contractor of the duty to verify compliance of Contract Documents with applicable laws and instead assigning direction to the Consultant/Owner when variances occur.
The clause establishes the Trade Contractor's fundamental obligation to perform the Work required by the Contract Documents for the identified Project, which is a core Work-execution duty.
Clause directly addresses the Contractor's failure to maintain required insurance and the Owner's right to obtain it and charge the cost back, governing insurance obligations under the Contract.
The clause specifies that the Owner may deduct the cost of substitute insurance from amounts due or becoming due to the Contractor, invoking payment mechanics.

The clause provides for extension of the Contract Time and corresponding adjustment of the Contract Time when delay events occur, functioning as a claims/adjustment mechanism for changes in the timing of performance.
The clause expressly states that the Contractor's Fee, the GMP and the Target Contract Price shall be adjusted as a result of the delay, directly administering the GMP/Target Cost mechanism.

The clause allocates responsibility for various delay-causing risks (labour disputes, fire, weather, subcontractor default, causes beyond the Contractor's control) by granting time and cost relief when such risks materialize, reflecting risk allocation between the parties.

The clause administers adjustments to the Profit Pool based on comparison between the Final Target Cost and Base Target Cost, directly relating to the target cost mechanism established under the Contract.

The clause provides for an extension of the Contract Time and reimbursement of costs to the Design-Builder as a result of delay caused by the Owner, effectively adjusting the Contract Time and cost consequences under the Contract's change/delay provisions.
The clause allocates responsibility for delay caused by the Owner's action or omission, assigning the resulting cost and time risk to the Owner rather than the Design-Builder.
The clause establishes the Consultant's duty to conduct reviews of the Work to verify completion status, which is a form of inspection/verification activity by an authorized party under the Contract.

The clause establishes that the Contract, once formed, constitutes a fixed baseline that can only be amended through the mechanisms set out in the Contract Documents, reflecting a lock-in principle where changes must follow prescribed procedures.

By stating that amendments to the Contract may only occur as provided in the Contract Documents, the clause implicitly points to the formal change mechanisms (e.g., Change Orders, Change Directives) governing adjustments to the Work and Contract Price.
The clause allocates to the Owner the right to reject a proposed Subcontractor or Supplier for reasonable cause, managing risk associated with the selection of parties performing the Work.
The clause requires the Owner to give notice of observed defects and deficiencies during the warranty period, which is part of the process for identifying and addressing non-conforming Work.

This clause is part of the Waiver of Claims provisions and establishes a procedural requirement for a party giving Notice in Writing of a claim to submit a detailed account, which is part of the formal claims process between the parties under the Contract.

The clause defines the general obligation of the Trade Contractor to supply labour, Products and services necessary for performance of the Work in accordance with the Contract Documents, establishing the scope and manner of executing the Work.
The clause directly addresses payment provisions, specifying that payments are subject to applicable lien legislation, which relates to payment compliance under Payment Legislation.

The clause allocates responsibility for damage arising from the Design-Builder's operations, while carving out exceptions for errors in the Owner's Statement of Requirements or acts/omissions of the Owner, thereby allocating and managing risk between the parties.
The clause establishes the Construction Manager's duty to control, direct, and supervise the Work to ensure conformity with the Contract Documents, a core work execution obligation.
Assigning total control and responsibility for conformity with the Contract Documents to the Construction Manager reflects an allocation of contractual responsibility for the Work.
The clause specifically addresses the discovery, reporting, and remediation of mould, a hazardous environmental contaminant, at the Place of the Project.

The clause allocates responsibilities between the Trade Contractor and Owner for reporting, mitigating, and resolving uncertainty about mould-related risks, including retaining an independent expert when the parties disagree.

The warranty period establishes the timeframe during which defective or non-conforming Work must be corrected under the Contract, tying directly to the concept of correction of defective Work post-completion.
The clause requires a statutory declaration of progress payment distribution to accompany each application for progress payment, directly governing payment application procedures.

The clause explicitly grants the Owner the right to make changes to the Work through additions, deletions, or revisions via Change Order or Change Directive, and to change the Contract Time by Change Order, which is the core mechanism for adjusting the Work and Contract Time under the Contract.
The clause establishes a formal mediation process, requiring parties to engage a Project Mediator under CCDC 40 rules to resolve unresolved disputes, which is a core dispute resolution mechanism.
The clause obligates the Design-Builder to provide inspection reports and test reports relating to the Work upon the Owner's request, directly implicating inspection processes and documentation.
Certificates and test reports referenced relate to quality assurance verification of compliance with the Contract Documents, supporting confirmation of Work quality.

The clause describes the Owner's review of Shop Drawings for conformity to the intent of the Contract Documents, a quality-assurance check on fabricated/detailed Product data prior to incorporation into the Work.

The clause allocates responsibility for errors or omissions in the Shop Drawings to the Design-Builder despite the Owner's review, clearly assigning risk for non-conformity unless expressly accepted via Change Order.
The provision addresses the consistency between Shop Drawings (part of the Construction Documents) and the Contract Documents, ensuring general arrangement and design intent are coordinated.
The clause references that a deviation from the Contract Documents can only be relieved if expressly accepted by the Owner through a Change Order, linking to the formal change process.

This clause is part of PART 6 CHANGES IN THE WORK and establishes the notice trigger for concealed or unknown conditions, which is a precursor step to adjustments in the Contract Price or Contract Time under the change provisions.

The clause allocates responsibility for identifying and notifying about concealed or differing physical conditions at the Place of the Work, establishing a mechanism for managing the risk of unforeseen site conditions before they are disturbed.
This clause obligates the Design-Builder to provide Design Services, establishing the design responsibility under the Contract.

This clause is part of GC 6.3 Change Directive, addressing how the cost of performing work attributable to a Change Directive is calculated, which is a mechanism for adjusting Work and Contract Price under formal change provisions.
The clause imposes a duty on the Trade Contractor for the proper performance of the Work, directly addressing how the Work must be carried out under the Contract Documents.

The clause ties the Trade Contractor's responsibility to the extent that the design and Contract Documents permit proper performance, linking performance obligations to design adequacy and coordination.

By limiting the Trade Contractor's warranty responsibility to what the design and Contract Documents allow, the clause allocates risk between design-related limitations and contractor performance obligations.
The clause requires the Contractor to furnish certificates and inspection reports relating to the Work, which is part of the inspection process under GC 2.3 REVIEW AND INSPECTION OF THE WORK.

The clause governs how the Construction Manager organizes and divides the Work among Subcontractors and Suppliers, addressing the performance and organization of the Work under the Contract Documents.

The clause requires the Owner, through the Consultant, to give notice of observed defects and deficiencies during the warranty period, directly relating to the identification of non-conforming or defective Work.
The clause grants the Construction Manager and Consultant authority to require inspection or testing of work whether fabricated, installed or completed, establishing an inspection right/procedure.
The clause gives authority to reject work that does not conform to the Contract Documents, directly addressing identification and rejection of non-conforming work.
Sub-clause .3 requires the Construction Manager and Consultant to prepare Change Orders and Change Directives as provided under the change provisions, directly governing formal changes to the Work.

The clause establishes a process for curing defaults, allocating responsibility for the defaulting party to correct performance issues within a defined framework, managing the consequences and risk of default under termination provisions.

The Consultant's review of Shop Drawings and other submittals is a quality assurance function to confirm compliance with the Construction Documents before Products are fabricated or incorporated into the Work.
Review of Shop Drawings and submittals ensures consistency and coordination between the Construction Manager's submissions and the Construction Documents.

This clause directly establishes the Owner's right to make changes to the Work, including additions, deletions, or revisions, via Change Order or Change Directive, and to adjust Contract Time by Change Order, which is the core mechanism defined under this code.

The clause requires PITs to use the Target Value Design process to optimize and coordinate the design in accordance with the Base Program, directly addressing design coordination and consistency with Contract Documents.

The clause requires PITs to collaborate with the PMT and other PITs on Project elements such as materials, systems, and equipment, and to meet regularly during the Target Value Design process—activities that occur during design development prior to the Construction Phase.

This clause is part of GC 6.6 Claims for a Change in Contract Price, governing the process for submitting interim and final accounts for claims arising from events affecting the Contract Price, which is a core mechanism of adjusting Work/Contract Price under the change provisions.
The clause preserves obligations regarding quality, correction and warranty of the Work performed prior to termination, ensuring corrective obligations survive contract termination.
The clause allocates ongoing responsibility for conformity and correction obligations even after termination, reflecting a risk allocation mechanism surviving termination.

The clause requires the Owner to designate a Payment Certifier to review applications for payment and certify the value of Design Services and of Work performed, directly establishing the payment certification mechanism.
The clause references certification of the value of Products delivered to the Place of the Work, touching on delivery of Products, though this is incidental to the payment certification function.

The clause allocates risk by having the Owner waive and release claims against the Construction Manager after Ready-for-Takeover, while carving out specific exceptions, thereby managing the parties' post-completion risk exposure.
The clause expressly preserves claims respecting toxic or hazardous substances, directly addressing an environmental risk exception to the general waiver.

This clause establishes the Owner's obligations to make progress payments, holdback payments, and final payment to the Contractor, referencing certification by the Consultant and compliance with Payment Legislation and holdback percentages.
The clause requires the Contractor to submit a schedule of values to facilitate evaluation of applications for payment, directly addressing payment application procedures.

The clause allocates and caps the liability of each party under the Contract, distinguishing between insured and uninsured losses and excluding indirect/consequential damages, which is a clear allocation and management of contractual risk.
The liability caps are expressly tied to the amount of insurance required under GC 11.1 – INSURANCE, linking the limitation of liability to insurance coverage levels.

The clause allocates the consequence of unremedied default by a Design/Construction Team member, establishing the SMT's right to terminate that member's participation, which is a risk allocation and management mechanism for default.

The clause addresses the Owner's rights to retain and use copies of design documents, and restricts further use without a license from the Consultant/Other Consultants, effectively governing ownership and usage rights over the Contract Documents.

The clause concerns consistency between the Construction Documents and the Contract Documents, requiring the Design-Builder to identify deviations to ensure compatibility with the Owner's requirements.
Accepted deviations from the Owner's Statement of Requirements are to be formalized through a Change Order, tying the clause to the Contract's change mechanism.

The clause preserves the Owner's obligation to pay the Fee for Services and reimbursable expenses despite the limitation of liability provisions, directly addressing payment obligations under the Contract.

The clause defines the scope of the Consultant's review of Shop Drawings as being limited to conformity with the design concept and general arrangement, addressing consistency between design services and construction documents.
The clause describes the nature and limits of the Consultant's review of Shop Drawings, which is a form of review/inspection procedure for compliance with the Contract Documents.

The clause requires the Contractor to compile a list of items to be completed or corrected and confirms that failure to list an item does not relieve the Contractor of its obligation to complete the Contract, directly addressing correction of incomplete or non-conforming Work.
The delivery of the list and application for Ready-for-Takeover to the Consultant and Owner for review constitutes an inspection/verification step in the takeover process.

The clause expressly addresses changes to the Work required by coordination with Other Contractors or Owner's forces, and directs that such changes be authorized and valued through Change Orders/Change Directives per GC 6.1-6.3.
The clause deals with coordination and integration of the work of Other Contractors or Owner's own forces with the Work, addressing interface compatibility issues.

This clause establishes the Contractor's fundamental obligation to perform the Work required by the Contract Documents at the Place of the Work, which is the core Work-execution duty under the Contract.
The clause governs the timing and amount of payment of portions of the Profit Pool at determined milestones, which is a payment mechanism under the Contract.
This clause establishes interest payable on unpaid amounts under the Contract, directly governing payment obligations and timing consequences for failure to pay.
Paragraph .2 applies interest to settlement amounts of claims resolved under Part 8 Dispute Resolution, linking the payment mechanism to the dispute resolution process.

The clause establishes payment timing obligations for the Owner to pay the Construction Manager within 28 days of receiving an application for payment, and requires compliance with Payment Legislation, which are core payment mechanics.

Several of the listed default triggers concern the Owner's failure to provide evidence of financing, the Consultant's failure to issue payment certificates, or the Owner's failure to pay certified or awarded amounts, all of which relate directly to the Contract's payment mechanics.

The clause requires the Contractor to promptly correct, at its own expense, defects or deficiencies in the Work appearing during the warranty period, directly addressing correction of defective/non-conforming Work.
The clause explicitly directs unresolved disagreements over the Contract Time adjustment to the dispute resolution provisions in Part 8, triggering the formal dispute process.
The clause deals with adjustment of Contract Time attributable to a change directive, which is part of the change management mechanism under the Contract.

This clause establishes supervisory representation requirements at the Place of the Work, addressing how communications and instructions are received and deemed to have been received by the Design-Builder's representative, which governs the organization and supervision of the Work.
The clause requires the Owner to provide evidence of financial arrangements to fulfill payment obligations under the Contract, directly relating to the Owner's capacity to meet payment provisions.

The clause establishes that the Contract, once formed, may only be amended through the mechanisms provided in the Contract Documents, mirroring the Design Lock-In concept that changes to an accepted baseline must follow the Contract's formal change provisions.

By stating that amendments to the Contract can only occur as provided in the Contract Documents, the clause implicitly channels any modifications through the Contract's formal change mechanisms such as Change Orders and Change Directives.
The clause references the Contractor's application for payment received by the Consultant and Owner, establishing part of the payment application process under GC 5.3 PAYMENT.

The clause allocates the risk of delay-causing events (labour disputes, fire, weather, and other causes beyond the Trade Contractor's control) between the parties, extending Contract Time but denying cost recovery unless the delay stems from actions of the Owner, Consultant or Construction Manager, thereby managing which party bears the consequences of these risks.

The listed causes of delay expressly include 'unusual delay by common carriers,' tying a schedule impact (extension of Contract Time) to delays in the delivery/transport of goods, which falls within the scope of delivery-related schedule impacts.

Positioned under Part 6 'Changes in the Work' and GC 6.5 'Delays,' the clause establishes a claim mechanism for adjusting the Contract Time based on qualifying delay events, consistent with the broader change/claim adjustment framework.

The clause allocates risk to the Owner by granting a right to terminate the Trade Contractor's right to continue the Work upon insolvency events (bankruptcy, assignment for benefit of creditors, receivership), effectively managing the Owner's exposure to the risk of contractor default due to financial failure.
The clause deals with valuation of Work performed under a Change Directive, pending final determination of the amount, directly governing adjustment mechanics for changes in the Work.
The clause specifies that the undisputed value of Change Directive work is eligible for inclusion in progress payments, directly addressing payment application and timing.
The clause grants the Consultant authority to reject work that does not conform to the Contract Documents, addressing identification and rejection of defective/non-conforming Work.
The clause gives the Consultant authority to require inspection or testing of work whether fabricated, installed or completed, establishing an inspection right.

The clause allocates responsibility by clarifying that the Consultant's exercise or non-exercise of authority does not create duties or liability toward the Contractor or others, managing risk of reliance on the Consultant's oversight.
The clause establishes the Owner's remedy and process for addressing the Construction Manager's default, allocating responsibility for non-compliance and providing a mechanism to manage that risk.

The clause addresses failure to properly perform the Work or comply with Contract requirements 'to a substantial degree,' triggering a correction period, analogous to correction of non-conforming performance.

The clause directs that modifications required due to legal variance or changes in law will be made via Change Order/Change Directive mechanisms under GC 6.1-6.3, tying compliance issues to the formal change process.
The clause allocates responsibility by relieving the Contractor of the duty to verify compliance of the Contract Documents with laws, shifting that risk/responsibility to the Consultant/Owner.

The clause assigns the Trade Contractor responsibility for the design, erection, operation, maintenance, and removal of Temporary Work necessary to perform the Work, establishing a duty governing how the Work is executed and supported.
The clause allocates sole responsibility to the Trade Contractor for Temporary Work, effectively assigning risk and accountability for its design, operation, and removal unless otherwise specified.

The clause is part of the negotiation, mediation and arbitration provisions, addressing timing requirements for a party to require immediate arbitration of a dispute, forming part of the formal dispute-resolution mechanism.

The clause addresses toxic and hazardous substances present at the Place of the Work and requires the Owner to prevent exposure exceeding legislated levels and to prevent property damage from such substances, which is an environmental protection obligation.
The clause allocates responsibility to the Owner for managing risks associated with pre-existing toxic or hazardous substances at the site, including exposure and property damage.

The clause establishes the Construction Manager's responsibility for proper performance of the Work, subject to the limits of the design and Contract Documents, which is a core Work-execution obligation.

The clause allocates responsibility for proper performance of the Work to the Construction Manager, qualified by the extent the design and Contract Documents permit such performance, effectively allocating risk for conformity between design and execution.

The clause establishes the Construction Manager's duty to notify the Consultant and arrange for inspections by authorities when work is designated for tests, inspections or approvals, directly governing inspection procedures and notification requirements.

This clause establishes a mutual indemnification obligation between Owner and Contractor, allocating responsibility for claims arising from negligence or failure to fulfill contract terms, which is a core risk allocation mechanism.

The clause establishes a broad waiver of claims among the Owner, Consultant, Contractor, and Other IPD Parties, allocating and limiting liability risk for the Project except for specifically enumerated categories such as willful misconduct, legal violations, warranty failures, payment claims, IP violations, insurable claims, third-party claims, and undiscovered substantial defects. This is a direct contractual mechanism for allocating and managing risk among the parties.

The clause allocates responsibility by clarifying that the Owner's Advisor's authority or exercise thereof does not create any duty or responsibility toward the Design-Builder or other parties, effectively limiting liability exposure.
The clause explicitly ties adjustment of the Contract Price and Contract Time for making good damage to the change provisions (GC 6.1, 6.2, 6.3), invoking the formal change mechanism.
The clause allocates responsibility for making good damage not caused by the Contractor, addressing the management of risk of damage to Work/property.
The clause requires the Contractor to make good/correct damage to the Work, similar to correction obligations for non-conforming conditions.

The clause addresses handling of the holdback amount required by lien legislation, including placement into a joint account, which is a payment/holdback compliance mechanism under Payment Legislation.
The clause addresses remediation and disposal of mould, a contamination/hazardous condition, caused by the Design-Builder's operations, fitting the environmental hazard concept.

The clause requires the Design-Builder to remediate the mould and 'make good any damage to the Work,' which parallels correction of non-conforming or damaging conditions caused by its own operations, at its own expense.
The clause allocates responsibility for mould caused by the Design-Builder's operations, requiring reimbursement of costs and indemnification, thereby assigning risk and liability for that condition.
The clause deals directly with toxic and hazardous substances at the place of the Work, requiring removal and disposal in accordance with applicable environmental legislation.

The clause allocates responsibility to the Contractor for hazardous substances brought onto site by the Contractor or those for whom it is responsible, including remediation costs and indemnification, reflecting risk allocation.
Requires the Contractor to make good any damage to the Work or property caused by the hazardous substances, similar to corrective work obligations.

The clause addresses disputes arising under the Contract outside the Consultant's authority and directs application of the negotiation, mediation, arbitration, and retention of rights procedures, establishing a dispute resolution pathway.

The clause allocates remedies and risk consequences to the Owner's default, giving the Trade Contractor the right to suspend or terminate if the default is not corrected within a specified period, reflecting risk allocation for non-performance.

The clause deals with errors, omissions, or inconsistencies in the Contract Documents and requires the Construction Manager to report them to the Consultant, directly addressing consistency and coordination of the design/contract documentation.
The clause allocates responsibility by stating the Construction Manager is not responsible for errors, omissions or inconsistencies in the Contract Documents, an explicit risk allocation provision.

The clause instructs that the Construction Manager 'shall not proceed with the work affected' until corrected information is received, directly governing how the Work is to be performed when document issues arise.

This clause governs the procedure following expiration of the negotiation/mediation period, addressing whether arbitration is binding and the parties' recourse to courts or other dispute resolution mechanisms, directly forming part of the dispute resolution process under GC 8.3.

The clause allocates responsibility for patent royalties and fees to the Contractor and requires the Contractor to hold the Owner harmless from claims arising from patent infringement, which is an allocation and management of contractual risk.
The clause governs applications for payment, including supporting documentation requirements, and specifically addresses payment for Products delivered but not yet incorporated into the Work.
The clause references Products delivered to the Place of the Work, tying payment to the delivery/transportation stage of Products prior to incorporation into the Work.

The clause governs progressive release of holdback amounts for subcontract work or Supplier-provided Products in Quebec, including certification by the Payment Certifier and timing of payment (30 calendar days), which is a payment mechanics provision including holdback and certification.

The clause expressly addresses toxic and hazardous substances at the Place of the Project, requiring the Owner to prevent exposure exceeding legislated levels and to prevent property damage from such substances, which is an environmental protection obligation.

The clause allocates responsibility to the Owner for managing risks associated with pre-existing toxic or hazardous substances at the site, assigning obligations to mitigate exposure and property damage.

The clause requires surety bonds issued by a licensed surety company to be maintained until Contract fulfillment, which is a mechanism for allocating and managing risk of non-performance under the Contract.

The clause governs holdback administration, requiring the Owner to place holdback funds in a joint account prior to expiry of the statutory holdback period, which is a payment mechanics/holdback compliance provision.
